prompts.wide:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: finished 16:9 pixel-art game environment background for Councillion / Future Counsel's underwater team-feud game.
Input image 1 is the APPROVED pixel-art style and palette reference. Input image 2 is only a rough LAYOUT reference; replace its crude flat geometric architecture with beautifully designed game artwork. Edit the environment into an original underwater law-court gameshow stage, preserving image 1's crisp, readable pixel clusters, medium-detail 16-bit illustration, deep blue/slate/teal palette, gentle cyan water and restrained antique gold.
OUTPUT ONLY THE EMPTY ENVIRONMENT. Remove ALL interface, all boards with numbers, all answer slots, all text, all characters, all benches/podiums, all buttons, all logos. Characters, podiums and interactive board are separate moving layers implemented in the game.
Composition: frontal establishing view into a submerged ancient courtroom built for a cheerful team game, camera at audience eye height slightly above a terraced slate floor. Two beautifully textured fluted stone columns around x=20% and 80%; weathered court pediment with a small scales-of-justice relief near top center; shells and modest coral around chipped bases; soft water visible behind arcades at the edges. Main center wall from x=24% to76%, y=18% to57% must be calm dark-blue stone, not detailed, to sit behind the real answer board. Lower 40% is open usable stage floor for foreground characters, with believable steps, chipped slate, subtle inlaid gold law motifs and faint pixelated caustics. Stage feels like a fun underwater court and game show, not a grim dungeon, not modern science fiction.
Craft: deliberate pixel clusters and confident silhouettes like image1, with varied stone chips, subdued plant motion implied, small warm brass court lanterns at the edges. Actual restrained pixel-art texture with visible coherent pixels, not hundreds of photorealistic bricks and not big flat color rectangles. Keep object density balanced; no dense seaweed, no giant gavel, no huge blank black doorway.
Lighting: luminous underwater blue with a few warm muted gold accents, enough contrast for bright pink shrimp sprites. Avoid photorealism, oil painting, 3D renders, neon tech, glossy UI, concept-art blur, noise, shallow depth of field, text or watermark. This is a polished GAME BACKGROUND, not a screenshot of a game.
prompts.benchAngle: Use case: precise-object-edit / style-transfer. Edit the reference environment into a genuinely different camera angle of THE SAME underwater Future Counsel court, preserving its architecture, proportions, blue slate, gold accents, medium-detail pixel clusters and cheerful clear lighting. It is an empty background plate for a 2D pixel game. Camera: lower, from the LEFT team bench position, looking diagonally toward the court's back wall on the RIGHT. Strong foreground-to-background depth and diagonal tile lines; close left-hand column and balcony molding at far LEFT, broad calm darker back-wall space on the RIGHT half for our interactive survey board. Lower 40% open floor for separate animated sprites; no benches, podiums, characters, lettering, numbers, interface or painted boards. Keep the same warm brass lanterns, carved law scales, shells, modest coral and chipped but cared-for slate architecture. Actual coherent 16-bit pixel illustration like reference, no realism, no blurry painting, no gritty high-frequency detail, no flat vector blocks. Landscape 16:9. Bright enough to play. This must be a new oblique shot, not simply a cropped or shifted copy of the reference.
prompts.hub: Use case: style-transfer. Edit the reference room into its matching entrance foyer: the MENU background for Future Counsel's cheerful underwater team-feud game. Same medium-detail crisp pixel-art style, same blue/teal slate, restrained warm gold, small shell/coral growth and underwater light. Wide 16:9 welcoming exterior-to-foyer view into a submerged ancient courthouse, TWO low curved stairways lead inward toward an open central team-court entrance with a small gold scales relief high above it. Frontal wide composition, lower camera, little warm amber court lanterns at far edges, large elegant fluted pillars frame the sides, ocean life and bubbles beyond the archways. Center stage floor in middle third remains clear for our animated avatar and two team stands; side regions at x=5–26% and x=75–95%, y=30–75% should have calm darker architecture so interactive menu text stays readable. No survey board, no repeated giant rectangles, no baked-in panels, no text, logos, characters, counters, benches, UI or buttons. Distinct foyer composition, not another shot of the same back wall. Use structured pixel clusters and sophisticated 16-bit game-art silhouettes matching the reference, not photorealistic or overly ornate fantasy art. Keep it lively, clear and friendly rather than gloomy or neon.
prompts.bench: Use case: background-extraction / precise-object-edit. From the visual language of this underwater court, create a SINGLE foreground TEAM BENCH prop for its pixel-art game: a long low slate counsel stand, frontal view with only a small amount of top surface visible. Transparent background, real alpha. No floor or scene behind it. Image itself should be wide landscape 3:1; the bench should occupy nearly the full canvas width with minimal transparent padding. Strong flat top edge where our separate shrimp/squid sprites will stand behind it. Blue/teal carved stone, antique gold edging, subtle chipped corners, five simple recessed front panels and one tasteful gold scales-of-justice emblem in the center, a tiny shell or coral at only one lower corner. Match reference pixel-cluster density and moderate game detail. Thick readable silhouette at small scale, believable dimensional top lip, no soft drop shadow beyond the object, no letters, labels, characters, buttons, realistic textures, neon light or glossy surfaces. This is the final deployable object sprite, not a mockup or a set of variants. Whole object fully visible, front baseline level and horizontal.
